title: Task-conditioned Deep Equilibrium maps
hypothesis: A shared contractive DEQ operator plus a compact rank-1 task coordinate can realize multiple stable fixed-point functions at lower actual inference bytes than per-task full maps, while maintaining fixed-point quality and solve effort.
physical_object: one shared contractive DEQ map h=tanh(Wh+Ux+b)
mirror_coordinate: one scalar per-task coordinate along a development-estimated shared task-bias direction
controls: shared DEQ with rank-1 native task bias residual
independent per-task full bias upper control
task: Synthetic 4D contractive tanh fixed point with task-specific bias. Infer task coordinates from support fixed points; evaluate heldout inputs, fixed-point residual, solver iterations, stability, bytes.

development.selection_metric: Estimate a single task-bias direction from four development tasks; no architecture/code-rank changes.

fresh.split: Each world has four development tasks defining the shared direction; eight aligned fresh task functions plus four full-vector out-of-span boundary functions. Each fresh task uses 128 support and 64 heldout inputs.

success_gate: For aligned fresh tasks in >=2/3 worlds, Mirror fixed-point output MSE <=1.05x full-bias control, max residual <=1e-6, spectral radius <=1, actual task-bank payload <=60% full-bias bank, and median solve iterations <= full control +1. Mirror-specific value additionally requires a measurable quality/byte/solve advantage over the matched native rank-1 task-bias residual.
failure_gate: FAIL if aligned quality/stability/storage gates fail in >=2/3 worlds, or Mirror is not better than the rank-1 native bias control on any relevant Pareto axis. Report out-of-span boundary separately.
boundaries: teacher aligned for four development tasks and separately perturbed out-of-span tasks
no language model or learned optimizer evidence
rank-1 code count is not independent capacity
